precepts.text: For Hezekiah he brought the shadow ten degrees backward on the sundial; time itself obeys him.
precepts.point: Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
For Hezekiah, “Isaiah the prophet cried unto the Lord: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.” Time itself obeys him.

The dew landing where he pleases, a rod budding overnight, the shadow going backward on the sundial: it is all the same infinite power. God did so that night for Gideon because he can do whatever he wants.

precepts.text: It is neither herb nor plaster that heals, but the word of the Most High, in whose hand is our healing.
precepts.point: Isaiah applies a lump of figs to the boil and Hezekiah recovers, showing that remedies and herbs go together with prayer, for healing is in the hand of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

precepts.why:
“For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but thy word, O Lord, which healeth all things.”

Isaiah said, “Take a lump of figs”, and they laid it on the boil, and Hezekiah recovered. Remedies and herbs go together with prayer. But it was not the figs that healed him. Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed, and the word came, “I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will heal thee.”

It is neither herb nor plaster that heals, but the word of the Most High. Our healing is in his hand.

precepts.text: A gift destroyeth the heart, which is why Hezekiah let his enemies in and showed them everything he owned.
precepts.point: Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in Isaiah 39.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

precepts.why:
“Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.”

Berodach-baladan king of Babylon “sent letters and a present unto Hezekiah.” The gift did its work. “Hezekiah hearkened unto them, and shewed them all the house of his precious things”, the silver, gold, spices, precious ointment and all his armour: “there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah shewed them not.”

A gift destroyeth the heart. Because of the present, Hezekiah trusted his enemies and let them in to see everything he owned, and that is why Isaiah declared it would all be carried into Babylon.

precepts.text: Isaiah's word is fulfilled when the children of Judah, including Daniel, are made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
precepts.point: Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in Isaiah 39.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

precepts.why:
The king of Babylon told Ashpenaz “the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes”, children without blemish, skilful in wisdom, able “to stand in the king’s palace”, to be taught “the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans.” “Now among these were of the children of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.”

That is Isaiah’s word fulfilled: “of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.” Daniel and his companions, of the king’s seed, were put under the master of the eunuchs and made eunuchs in that palace.

precepts.text: Some are born eunuchs and some are made eunuchs of men, as Daniel and his companions were made eunuchs after they were grown.
precepts.point: Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in Isaiah 39.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

precepts.why:
“For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men.”

Some are born eunuchs and some are made eunuchs of men. Daniel and his companions were made eunuchs of men, after they were grown, when they were carried to Babylon. So Isaiah’s word that Hezekiah’s sons “shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon” came to pass as it was spoken.

precepts.text: Hezekiah made a pool and a conduit and brought water into the city, the water system he now used against the siege.
precepts.point: He sets captains over the people and comforts them: be strong and courageous, for there be more with us than with him; with him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God to help us and fight our battles.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
Kings records “the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made a pool, and a conduit, and brought water into the city”. Hezekiah had built a water system for Jerusalem, and now he used it against the siege.

When “Sennacherib king of Assyria came, and entered into Judah, and encamped against the fenced cities”, Hezekiah took counsel “to stop the waters of the fountains which were without the city”, and the people “stopped all the fountains, and the brook that ran through the midst of the land, saying, Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?” The water came into the city, and the enemy outside found none.

He also “built up all the wall that was broken, and raised it up to the towers, and another wall without, and repaired Millo in the city of David, and made darts and shields in abundance.” Our people are resourceful and skilled, doing the work themselves.

precepts.text: Isaiah tells Hezekiah to set his house in order for he shall die, and after Hezekiah prays the Lord adds fifteen years to his life and defends the city.
precepts.point: Then Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord does not come upon them in his days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
Kings gives the fuller account of the sickness. “In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death.” Isaiah came and said, “Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.” Hezekiah “turned his face to the wall, and prayed unto the Lord”, “I beseech thee, O Lord, remember now how I have walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart”, “And Hezekiah wept sore.”

Before Isaiah was out of the middle court the word came: “I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will heal thee”. “And I will add unto thy days fifteen years; and I will deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will defend this city for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.”

That is the benefit done to him. And yet “Hezekiah rendered not again according to the benefit done unto him; for his heart was lifted up: therefore there was wrath upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.” When things go well, do not get puffed up and make it about yourself. “Notwithstanding Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord came not upon them in the days of Hezekiah.”

precepts.text: The sign is the shadow returning ten degrees backward on the sundial of Ahaz, a thing only the Most High could do.
precepts.point: Then Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord does not come upon them in his days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
Chronicles says only that the Lord “gave him a sign.” Kings shows what it was. Hezekiah asked, “What shall be the sign that the Lord will heal me”? Isaiah answered, “shall the shadow go forward ten degrees, or go back ten degrees?”

Hezekiah said, “It is a light thing for the shadow to go down ten degrees: nay, but let the shadow return backward ten degrees.” “And Isaiah the prophet cried unto the Lord: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.” The shadow returning backward on the sundial of Ahaz was a thing only the Most High could do.

That was the benefit Hezekiah was shown, and it is why his lifted-up heart afterward brought wrath, until he humbled himself.

precepts.text: The same account of Hezekiah's sickness and Isaiah's word that he set his house in order.
precepts.point: The sign given was the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz brought back ten degrees. The prophet had told them it was a light thing to make the sundial go forward ten degrees, so instead the sun returned backward ten degrees as the sign to Hezekiah.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

precepts.why:
The same account is recorded in Kings, word for word: “In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death. And the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz came to him, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.”

Two witnesses to Hezekiah’s sickness and to Isaiah’s word that he set his house in order, for he would die and not live. It was after this that Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall, reminded the Most High how he had “walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart”, and wept sore, and the Most High heard the prayer, saw the tears, and added fifteen years to his days.

precepts.text: The parallel record of the sundial sign brought backward ten degrees.
precepts.point: The sign given was the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz brought back ten degrees. The prophet had told them it was a light thing to make the sundial go forward ten degrees, so instead the sun returned backward ten degrees as the sign to Hezekiah.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

precepts.why:
Kings gives the fuller record of the sign of the sundial. “And Isaiah said, This sign shalt thou have of the Lord, that the Lord will do the thing that he hath spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten degrees, or go back ten degrees?” Hezekiah was given the choice, and answered, “It is a light thing for the shadow to go down ten degrees: nay, but let the shadow return backward ten degrees.”

It was a light thing to make the sundial go forward ten degrees, so instead the sun returned backward ten degrees as the sign to Hezekiah. “And Isaiah the prophet cried unto the Lord: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.” That is the sign of Isaiah 38:8, “the shadow of the degrees, which is gone down in the sun dial of Ahaz, ten degrees backward”, the Lord’s proof that he would do the thing he had spoken: add fifteen years to Hezekiah and deliver the city out of the hand of the king of Assyria.

precepts.text: Isaiah told Hezekiah that all that is in thine house shall be carried into Babylon, and thy sons shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
precepts.point: Nebuchadnezzar carried those vessels into the land of Shinar to the house of his god and put them in his treasure house. This came to pass exactly as the prophets had warned.

note.label: Daniel 1: The Best of Israel Carried to Babylon

precepts.why:
This came to pass exactly as the prophets had warned. When the men from Babylon had seen everything in Hezekiah's house, Isaiah told him, “Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store unto this day, shall be carried into Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord. And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”

Hezekiah had shown them all: “there is nothing among my treasures that I have not shewed them.” So when Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, took Jehoiakim and carried part of the vessels of the house of God to the treasure house of his god, it was the word Isaiah spoke to Hezekiah being fulfilled, and the sons of Judah were to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

moments.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Hezekiah was one of the very few righteous kings, so righteous that the Most High extended his life, and Manasseh his son reigned in his stead.
Kings gives more detail on the northern kingdom and Chronicles on the southern, so the class reads both accounts of Manasseh.
